chunks: And with this chain of narration, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Indeed, the servant attains the rank of the one who fasts and prays (at night) through good character.

key_terms.القائِمِ: The one who stands in prayer (specifically night prayer/Qiyam)

ai.seo_question: How can good character earn the same reward as fasting and night prayer?
ai.summary: In *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to emphasize that *husn al-khuluq* (excellent character) is not merely a social virtue but a transformative spiritual practice equivalent to the rigorous acts of *sawm* (fasting) and *qiyam* (night prayer). This aligns with the Shia tradition, particularly in the teachings of Imam al-Rida, which elevates moral refinement as the practical manifestation of faith, often cited alongside the concept of *adab* as the crown of the wise. The narration underscores that consistent ethical conduct can compensate for or even surpass the spiritual merit of ritual devotion when performed with sincerity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-97 According to the same documentation, God’s Prophet (S) said, “
A servant (i.e. a person) will attain the rank of one who fasts and stays up at night through being good-tempered.”
